method: 18 file-group classifiers + per-group no-theatre skeptic challenge; disputed stamps reclassified fail-closed to LLM-ATTESTED; workflow wf_044be42d-098, 36 agents; amended 2026-08-30 (round-2): attention_gate.py citations re-derived after the Phase 0.1 insertion via difflib line mapping, writer-control row added class-at-birth

rows.control: RepoAdapter write discipline: PR-only mutation, never auto-push to a protected branch, read/write scope separation
rows.evidence: This is a docstring contract on a typing.Protocol; Protocols are structural interfaces with no runtime enforcement, the concrete implementation is target-supplied, and nothing in the core checks that create_branch/open_pull_request are the only mutation paths or that credentials are least-privilege.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing in this file or the core — an adapter implementation (or the lane driving it) that pushes directly to a protected branch violates only prose; enforcement would have to live in platform branch protection or the broker/tool-policy layers outside this seam declaration.

rows.control: KnowledgeAdapter write-back constraint: affinity nodes provisional until a human endorses, written only via PR into the target's .kin
rows.evidence: Docstring contract only; write_affinity's promise that nodes stay unflagged/provisional and land via PR is enforced by no core code — the implementation and the endorsing step are outside the seam.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing mechanical here — an implementation could write endorsed-looking nodes or bypass the PR path and the core would not notice.

rows.control: IdpAdapter authentication contract: verified claims, no local passwords, JIT-unprivileged default role
rows.evidence: authenticate/claims_to_capabilities are interface stubs; the actual credential verification, the no-local-passwords rule, and the unprivileged JIT default are docstring promises fulfilled (or not) by the target-supplied implementation.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing in the core — a permissive or fabricated claims_to_capabilities implementation feeds the RoleModel unauthenticated capability sets; the core's only mechanical backstop is the catalog intersection in roles.py.

rows.control: ArtifactSink content-addressing contract (put returns a content address the ledger references by digest)
rows.evidence: Docstring promise on an interface stub; nothing in this file verifies the returned string is actually a content address of the stored bytes — downstream digest re-verification (where it exists in manifest/evidence consumers) is the real control, not this seam.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing here — an implementation returning a mutable location or a wrong digest is caught only if and where a consumer re-derives the digest against fetched bytes.

rows.control: ADAPTER_PROTOCOLS declared-set pin
rows.evidence: tests/test_adapters.py pins the tuple from outside the module (DECLARED_SEAMS equality at line 104, undeclared-Protocol refusal at line 125, count pin at line 140, ADAPTER_KINDS/KIND_TO_PROTOCOL parity at line 151), so a seam cannot be added or removed as a side effect.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: The pytest assertions fail on any drift regardless of what a lane writes — provided the suite runs (make ship) before the change lands.

rows.control: vocabulary_digest grouping key (redefined codes are digest-visible)
rows.evidence: sha256 over the canonical JSON of code+predicate pairs; frequency_table groups by it so incommensurable counts cannot be pooled.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host hashing of a source-code constant.

rows.control: audit_run run_id requirement
rows.evidence: Empty normalized run_id raises AuditError rather than auditing anonymously.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host emptiness check.

rows.control: audit_run fail-closed on unrecognized dispositions
rows.evidence: verdict_rank is called on both verdict.disposition and promotion_disposition before any predicate (L235-236), so a malformed artifact raises instead of producing a partial audit; a silent skip is never confusable with clean.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host lookup raising VerdictError.

rows.control: Audit predicate suite (uncovered-mass-shipped, verdict-overclaim, scope-union-gap, oracle-frame-untested, uncoded-pass residual)
rows.evidence: Each code is a deterministic predicate over typed artifacts (L153-211), pass-family gated at L239, with uncoded-pass as the mandatory residual (L251-252) so silence is distinguishable from a stale vocabulary.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Pure host predicates — but non-gating BY DESIGN (they can never block anything), and they inherit the trust roots of their inputs: coverage statuses, receipts, and scope claims are lane-authored.

rows.control: frequency_table malformed-row refusal and denominator-attached counts
rows.evidence: Rows with missing digest/run or a code outside AUDIT_CODES raise AuditError (L277-278); counts are grouped per vocab_digest with runs_observed attached and no rank ever emitted.

rows.evidence: Same ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ regex gate used for pattern, target, and input digest fields.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Regex fullmatch in host code.

rows.control: pattern definition validity (pattern-id-missing/duplicate, -version-missing, -artifact-digest-invalid, -qualification-evidence-digest-invalid, -mechanism-empty)

rows.control: plan identity presence (build-plan-id-missing, build-plan-version-missing)

rows.control: target freshness binding (build-plan-target-digest-mismatch)

rows.control: build-input freshness binding (build-plan-input-digest-mismatch)

rows.evidence: Lines 437-446 re-derive current phase content digests from the provenance bundle and require the plan's recorded map to match exactly and cover all three required phases.

rows.evidence: Lines 447-452 compile every step intent backreference and oracle link into ProvenanceClaims and run the full verify_intent_provenance gate, prefixing any issue into this report.

rows.evidence: Lines 491-512 compute the set of all product+architecture item backreferences and flag every one not claimed by any step, forcing complete intent coverage.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Set difference over host-derived backreference sets; silently dropping a requirement from the plan is mechanically visible.

rows.evidence: Lines 518-536 require at least one oracle link, dedupe pairs, and require each expectation to be a real product/architecture item and each oracle a real operational-maturity item.

rows.control: bidirectional oracle coverage (build-plan-oracle-coverage-missing, build-plan-operational-item-unused)
rows.evidence: Lines 537-546 flag every product expectation lacking an oracle and every operational item no link uses, so testing/monitoring intent cannot be silently orphaned.

rows.control: fail-closed readiness aggregation (ready iff zero issues)
rows.evidence: ready = not unique — any accumulated issue blocks readiness; no waiver or severity override exists in this layer.

rows.control: Gate predicate: satisfied only with zero gaps/failures/integrity issues
rows.evidence: ChecklistReport.satisfied is the conjunction 'not gaps and not failures and not integrity_issues' (lines 100-102); there is no waiver parameter and no prose input to the predicate.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: A pure boolean over host-computed tuples; an LLM cannot flip it without eliminating each underlying defect through the mechanical checks above.

rows.control: Duplicate required-item detection (verify_checklist)
rows.evidence: Normalized required ids are deduplicated and any collapse records the integrity issue 'checklist-required-item-duplicate' (lines 127-140), which makes satisfied False (line 102).
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Tuple-length comparison in host code over the supplied definition; not overridable by model output.

rows.control: Result-id missing/duplicate refusal (verify_checklist indexing)
rows.evidence: An empty normalized result id records 'checklist-item-id-missing' (lines 145-147) and a repeated id records 'checklist-item-duplicate:<id>' and is not indexed (lines 148-150); both are integrity issues that fail the report.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Dict-membership checks in host code; an LLM cannot satisfy an item twice or anonymously.

rows.control: Unknown-result containment (checklist-item-outside-definition)
rows.evidence: A result whose id is not in the required set is recorded as a report and can never satisfy a required item (lines 152-153); only ids in the required tuple are iterated for satisfaction (line 155).
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Set-membership in host code; emitting extra passing items cannot substitute for a required one.

rows.control: Missing-required-item gap (checklist-item-missing)
rows.evidence: Every required id with no indexed result appends a gap (lines 156-159); gaps make satisfied False (line 102), so an unchecked item stays visible instead of defaulting to pass.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: The absence is computed by host code from the supplied results; silence from an LLM lane produces a blocking gap, not a pass.

rows.control: recorded_at presence gate (checklist-item-recorded-at-missing)
rows.evidence: recorded_at <= 0 is a gap (lines 163-165), and from_dict coerces unparseable values to 0 (lines 66-70) so malformed timestamps fail closed into the gap.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Integer comparison in host code. NOTE: the VALUE is caller-asserted — the module docstring (lines 8-11) concedes it cannot prove when the item was persisted; an LLM-authored result can stamp any positive number, so this enforces presence of a claim, and write-ordering truth belongs to the append-only sink.

rows.control: Per-item evidence chain: missing/digest-mismatch/subject-mismatch
rows.evidence: Absent evidence is a gap (lines 168-170); a digest that does not re-derive is integrity issue 'checklist-item-evidence-digest-mismatch' (lines 171-173); evidence not binding the exact authority_body — normalized item id, subject_digest, passed, detail, recorded_at (lines 44-53) — is 'checklist-item-evidence-subject-mismatch' (lines 174-176). Either issue blocks satisfaction (line 180).
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Digest math and field equality in host code catch tamper and cross-subject replay mechanically; but the digests are unkeyed, so the lane that authors an item can mint self-consistent evidence for a passed=True claim — the control proves the record was not altered or replayed, never that the observation happened.

rows.control: Negative evidence is unwaivable (checklist-item-failed)
rows.evidence: Any result with passed=False is recorded as a failure regardless of its evidence state (lines 178-179), and the docstring contract makes failures and integrity issues non-convertible into waivers (lines 88-91); satisfied requires all three defect lists empty (line 102).
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Boolean check in host code — a recorded failure cannot be argued away. The passed bit itself, however, is authored by whoever produced the result; an LLM lane that decides to write passed=True is only caught if some other control verified the underlying observation.

rows.control: Unknown-status coercion to GAP (fail-closed status normalization)
rows.evidence: normalize_status maps any string outside KNOWN_STATUSES to STATUS_GAP, and InventoryRow.__post_init__ (lines 122-123) forces every row through it, so an unrecognized status can never read as done.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Deterministic string mapping; a typo'd or invented status degrades to least-complete regardless of author.

rows.control: DECLARED-is-not-complete rule (claim without proof does not close a row)
rows.evidence: is_complete returns True only for PROVED or EXCUSED; DECLARED, PARTIAL, GAP all read as open, and meet (lines 87-99) aggregates multi-dimension rows to their weakest rung.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: The predicate is host code — but nothing in this module verifies that a row STAMPED "PROVED" was actually proved (see next row); the mechanical rule only distinguishes the strings.

rows.control: PROVED/EXCUSED status authenticity (the fact behind the string)
rows.evidence: InventoryRow.from_dict accepts the status string from whatever the KnowledgeAdapter seam returns; `source` is a free-form pointer never dereferenced or digest-checked, so a row claiming PROVED carries no proof binding in this module.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing: if an LLM lane (or LLM-authored document a parser reads) writes status=PROVED or EXCUSED, launch_ready counts the row complete — the host merely records the claim.

rows.control: Launch-readiness predicate (green only when every row terminal-complete)
rows.evidence: launch_ready computes ready = not inventory.open_rows() and returns the exact blocking rows, so the verdict is falsifiable and reproducible from the row set.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Pure computation over rows — but its inputs are the attested statuses above, so the gate's real strength is bounded by the PROVED-authenticity row (demotion candidate as deployed).

rows.control: Empty-inventory-is-not-ready guard (vacuous-truth trap)
rows.evidence: launch_ready forces ready=False when require_nonempty (default True) and the inventory has no rows, so "nothing enumerated" never reads as "everything done"; a caller can disable it with require_nonempty=False, which is a caller-side waiver.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Deterministic host check; bypass requires the calling code to pass the explicit keyword, not model persuasion.

rows.control: Structural substance test (non-string / thin field never substantive)
rows.evidence: is_substantive requires an actual str meeting min_chars trimmed length AND min_tokens word-like tokens (regex line 51), rejecting None, numbers, containers, and punctuation runs — a purely structural, injection-resistant predicate.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Deterministic regex/length math; a crafted submission cannot talk its way past it, though by design any substantive-looking filler text passes — semantic adequacy is explicitly not enforced here.

rows.control: Per-field substance rule (content elsewhere cannot satisfy a missing field)
rows.evidence: SubstanceRequirement.__call__ reads exactly submission[field] via spec_for (conditional selectors compared normalized, lines 160-166) and emits a FieldGap when the single field fails its spec.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host code evaluates the one field mechanically; the field lists and thresholds are per-target data, so which fields are required at all is authored configuration.

rows.control: Rule-registration collision guard (empty or duplicate rule id fails loud)
rows.evidence: ComprehensivenessGate.register raises ComprehensivenessError on a blank id (line 212) or an already-registered id (line 214), so a gate rule can never be silently dropped or shadowed.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Python raises at registration time regardless of any model.

rows.control: Deterministic intake verdict (comprehensive iff zero gaps)
rows.evidence: evaluate runs every registered rule in order and sets VERDICT_NEEDS_INFO whenever any gap fired; same submission always yields the same verdict with no LLM in the loop (module docstring's stated design goal, borne out by the code).
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Pure predicate over discrete fields; the only authored surface is the rule set itself, supplied as per-target data by whoever configures the gate.

rows.control: Blank excuse rule matches nothing (cannot excuse everything by accident)
rows.evidence: ExcuseRule.matches returns False when _has_predicate() (lines 229-238) finds no predicate set, so an empty rule can never bucket an orphan.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Deterministic predicate check — but excuse rules are per-target DATA with target-chosen excused=True; if an LLM lane authors the rule list it can excuse any orphan with a one-line prefix rule, so the waiver authority behind this control is a demotion candidate to LLM-ATTESTED.

rows.control: Unclassified-orphan fail-closed default (no rule match = unexcused gap)
rows.evidence: ExcuseClassifier.classify returns label UNCLASSIFIED_LABEL (line 265) with excused=False for any orphan no supplied rule matches, so absence of a rule can never hide an orphan.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host code sets excused=False deterministically; only an authored excuse rule (data, see previous row) can flip an orphan to excused.

rows.control: Unresolved caller-edge quarantine (never a match, never silently dropped)
rows.evidence: forward_contract routes edges with empty path (CallEdge.resolved, lines 138-139) into the separate `unresolved` bucket and reverse_contract (line 395) excludes them from called_keys, so an unresolvable call can neither satisfy nor be counted as a provider match.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Deterministic set logic over adapter-supplied inventories; if the inventories are authored by an LLM lane the whole diff is over attested data (demotion candidate), but the bucketing itself cannot be talked past.

rows.control: Forward contract break detection (caller edge with no provider)
rows.evidence: forward_contract flags any resolved edge whose normalized (method, path) key is absent from provider_keys as a break; ForwardReport.ok (lines 320-321) is false whenever breaks exist.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Pure set difference; enforcement depends only on the truthfulness of the caller/provider inventories supplied through RepoAdapter seams (per-target code, not this module).

rows.control: Reverse contract orphan detection (provider operation with no caller)
rows.evidence: reverse_contract flags every endpoint whose key appears in no resolved caller edge as an orphan and classifies it; ReverseReport.ok (lines 351-352) is false while any unexcused orphan remains, and ContractReport.ok (lines 418-419) ANDs both directions.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Mechanical set diff; the escape hatch is not the code but the excuse-rule data (next row).

rows.control: declared_role recorded before the run (role ordering)
rows.evidence: The docstring names the ordering as THE control ('a role inferred after seeing the result is a rationalization'), but nothing in this module can verify when the declaration happened relative to the run — ordering is entirely the authoring lane's word.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing — a lane can declare the role after seeing the baseline result and the classifier cannot tell.

rows.evidence: Missing test_id, undeclared/unknown role, or baseline_result outside the closed set all return CONTROL_ROUTE_HUMAN (lines 167-174) — fail-closed to a human, never a pass.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Closed-enum host checks; every ambiguous input routes to a human.

rows.control: red-now test already green is a recognition-check, not a pass
rows.evidence: baseline_result==passed on a declared red-now returns CONTROL_RECOGNITION_CHECK, which verify_correction turns into a gate_reason (line 386). Note baseline_result is caller-supplied; it must come from host test execution for this to hold.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host branch; the disposition gates to a human rather than passing.

rows.control: red-now satisfied only when the failure is ON the defect

rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing — relabeling an unrelated failure as 'defect' converts route-human into satisfied.

rows.control: red-now failing away from the defect / relation unrecorded routes to a human
rows.evidence: Both the 'unrelated' and missing failure_relation branches return CONTROL_ROUTE_HUMAN — fail-closed on ambiguity.

rows.control: green guard failing on unrelated behavior is a suspected over-constraint that stops; a guard can never be reclassified as forcing

rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Structural: the function has no branch that repurposes a guard; every non-satisfied green-now outcome gates or routes to a human.

rows.control: green-now failed on defect-related behavior / relation unrecorded routes to a human
rows.evidence: Both remaining green-now branches return CONTROL_ROUTE_HUMAN.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host branch, fail-closed.

rows.evidence: verify_correction(None) returns an unsatisfied report with the gap; satisfied requires all four failure buckets empty (line 313).
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host None-check.

rows.control: defect id required (correction-defect-id-missing)
rows.evidence: Blank defect_id gaps the record.

rows.control: controls missing with a baseline is a gap
rows.evidence: Empty classification list with baseline_available gaps correction-controls-missing.

rows.control: positive control must be observed — a declared green-now must exist
rows.evidence: No green-now declaration among classifications gaps positive-control-unobserved.

rows.control: reproduction record present with a recorded, known result
rows.evidence: Missing record or blank result gaps; a result outside the closed REPRODUCTION_RESULTS set is an integrity failure (lines 413-420).
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host closed-enum checks.

rows.control: reproduction must be for this defect (reproduction-defect-mismatch)

rows.control: not-reproduced gates — no repair authorized against the original hypothesis

rows.control: reproduction-occurred veracity (result='reproduced' reflects a real triggered fault)
rows.evidence: The reproduced path's inputs — result, environment_id, disposable_environment — are producer-attested fields under an UNKEYED digest (authority_body, line 217); nothing in this module verifies any reproduction actually ran, so a fabricated 'reproduced' record with a self-computed digest passes.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing — the module explicitly does no test execution (line 34); the claim is only as good as the external producer, which may be a lane.

rows.control: reproduction environment must be disposable
rows.evidence: disposable_environment is a self-reported boolean; False is a failure but nothing verifies a True claim against any real environment property.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Nothing — the host branches on a flag the producer authors.

rows.control: reproduction environment id recorded
rows.evidence: Blank environment_id gaps reproduction-environment-unrecorded.
rows.llm_disobedience_answer: Host string check.
